scope: Exact covariance-spectrum KL formula evaluated in FP64 for the declared independent-window block-center Gaussian alternative; no interval-certified numeric bounds.

Only public manifest fields, full sampled Grams, intervals and valid-row calendars enter; no mean, signal energy, observed noise, injected variance, true bit or physical fading realization is used.
For each candidate D(P_signal||P_null)=sum(lambda/variance-log1p(lambda/variance)); variance=sample_rate/10^(total_nominal_triplet_CN0/10). Actual shaped energy and public erasures enter through G.

Binary KL thresholds are necessary presence conditions, not sufficient correct-bit performance, empirical false-admission calibration or a duration recommendation. Bit discrimination and search uncertainty are separate losses.

Any comparison C/N0 is supplied externally and is not validated here. Its difference from a necessary crossing is not a proved receiver inefficiency or an achievable improvement.

g001.interpretation: Model-based necessary-information values are lower limits under different assumptions; compare with the measured interval descriptively only. They do not predict achievable correct-bit reception.

g01.interpretation: Model-based necessary-information values are lower limits under different assumptions; compare with the measured interval descriptively only. They do not predict achievable correct-bit reception.

g1.interpretation: Model-based necessary-information values are lower limits under different assumptions; compare with the measured interval descriptively only. They do not predict achievable correct-bit reception.

interpretation.acceptance_probability: correct_accepted / conditional noise trials, with duration and covariance-window choice identified in each source configuration.
interpretation.conditional_trials: Trials resample noise conditional on each listed sampled physical path; totals across paths are descriptive only and no binomial confidence interval is pooled across paths.
interpretation.confidence_claims: No channel-population confidence guarantee is made from these fixed-path conditional trials.
interpretation.timing_confound: Aligned screen cases preserve campaign seed roots, sample rate and nominal channel parameters for same-rate/index pairs while forcing known initial time (GPS 0 ms, 0 ms region/offset, audio 0 ms). Timing information changes; capture padding/timeline can also change, so this is not a decoder-only paired gain. High-rate nominal-time screens have unsearched timing ambiguity and should not be read as Doppler-width limits. Low-rate nominal timing banks are an approximate search, not a fully blind exhaustive acquisition proof. Separately finer-Fs cases use different path roots.
interpretation.unknown_information: The necessary information crossings are known-noise, specified covariance-model calculations; they are not receiver-achievable or correct-bit guarantees.

key_observations: At B=0.001 Hz, 86,400 s, GUI inner rate 0.036 Hz and J=64, the fixed-path conditional score is 83/128 accepted at -28 dB-Hz and 128/128 at -26 dB-Hz; at -28, J=16 and J=32 Gaussian-window scores are 73/128 and 79/128 (OU J=32 is 78/128).
At B=0.01 Hz, J=64 gives 64/128 at -24 dB-Hz; B=0.1 Hz gives 21/128 at -14 and 123/128 at -12. These are distinct sampled conditions with varying durations/rates.

At B=0.001 Hz and -28 dB-Hz, assumed covariance width 0.5x and 2x yields 73/128 and 64/128 respectively, versus matched width 83/128; the small fixed path set does not establish robust mismatch tolerance.

For B=0.1 Hz at -14 dB-Hz, J=32 with 4-second, 1-second and 0.5-second base blocks produced 21/128, 21/128 and 11/128. These use the same path seed fields but different block-statistic inputs; this is a paired-seed refinement screen, not identical observation-array parity.

The B=0.01 Hz slow-rate screen scores 5/128 at -26 dB-Hz versus 2/128 for the higher-rate J=32 screen, but manifests show different key/channel seeds, so the small difference is not a paired rate effect.

The static-FFT stable-day controls (24h, GUI rate .036 Hz) at 1/10/30 Hz center score 152/256, 134/256 and 134/256 at -35 dB-Hz, then 256/256 at -30; long-duration stable controls at .005/.05/.1 Hz center score 94/256, 118/256 and 121/256 at -63, then 256/256 at -60. These share duration/rate within cohort, but use distinct sample rates and unpaired physical path roots.

For the high-width known-initial-time aligned screens, B=10 Hz gives 64/64 at +5 dB-Hz; B=30 Hz gives 64/64 at +15 dB-Hz (its finer-block cohort gives 63/64 at +10). These are conditional trials on four sampled paths and explicitly assume initial-time knowledge.

For fast delay at -10 dB-Hz, nominal-time receiver conditions score 32/128 for modeled 0, 6 and 7 ms; the 7 ms path with receiver delay mismatch scores 8/128. Artificial known-initial-time aligned sets score 64/64 for 0, 6 and 7 ms; timing truth, sample timeline/padding and cohorts preclude interpreting this as pure acquisition gain.

CPU FP32, CPU FP64 and CUDA FP32 matched-input window scores preserve ranking and gate decisions across 1,024 score rows per comparison; max absolute log-score delta is recorded below. These runs were under concurrent load; timing is not an isolated speed comparison.
limitations: Screen rates, durations, sampling rates, and window sizes vary across the B-width sweep; the plot is a feasibility screen, not a controlled rate/duration comparison.
The OU and Gaussian-window likelihoods use distinct temporal models; observed differences are model-fit evidence, not a universal ranking.
The path samples are few and fixed per condition. The many conditional noise trials do not increase the number of independent physical paths.

The plotted 24-hour and 2.4-hour labels are requested active durations; actual simulated captures run longer due to waveform rounding, timing lead and retained tails. Stable long-duration controls are 850 days requested.
High-rate original nominal-time rows have an unsearched timing dimension; aligned rows condition on known initial time and cannot be used as an apples-to-apples acquisition result.
The nominal timing/receiver timing mismatch cohort is not an aligned waveform pair; acquisition-versus-channel loss cannot be isolated by direct subtraction.
Recorded runtime values were collected under concurrent workload; no CPU/GPU speedup claim is made.
